paper_metadata.title: Regulating the strength and ductility of a cold rolled FeCrCoMnNi high-entropy alloy via annealing treatment

evidence.quote: An equiatomic FeCrCoMnNi high-entropy alloy was processed by cold rolling and then isochronous annealing treatments.
The single phase FeCrCoMnNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) with equiatomic ratio was one of the widely investigated face-centered cubic (FCC) HEAs [1].

The FeCrCoMnNi alloy ingot with equiatomic ratio was fabricated through vacuum induction melting high-purity Fe (99.95%), Cr (99.99%), Co (99.98%), Mn (99.5%) and Ni (99.995%) in high-purified argon atmosphere.

It can also be seen from Fig. 1 that the ductility of the specimens CR0-A T-1073-1 and CR0-A T-1173-1 is better than that of the as-cast sample, and the yield stresses of all the samples are higher than that of the as-cast sample.

process_steps.input_state: high-purity elemental Fe, Cr, Co, Mn, Ni

evidence.quote: The FeCrCoMnNi alloy ingot with equiatomic ratio was fabricated through vacuum induction melting high-purity Fe (99.95%), Cr (99.99%), Co (99.98%), Mn (99.5%) and Ni (99.995%) in high-purified argon atmosphere.
The alloy ingot was homogenization annealed at a temperature of 1273 K for 2 hours.
Then cold rolling process was conducted on the homogenization annealed ingot with a thickness reduction of ~0.9.

evidence.quote: sealed in vacuum tubes, followed by isochronous annealing at 773, 873, 923, 973, 1073 and 1173 K for 1 h, and then air cooled to the room temperature.

phases_and_microstructures.name: long-range ordered structure
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 773 K

evidence.quote: No precipitation particle was observed in the sample CR0-A T-773-1 after one hour annealing treatment at 773 K, as shown in Fig. 3b. While the corresponding SAED pattern indicates the formation of long-range ordered structure

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr-rich precipitate
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K

evidence.quote: Segregation of Cr element and lacking of Ni element can be detected in the precipitation particles, and the Cr-rich phase was distributed along the dislocations inside the grains.

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr-rich precipitate
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K

evidence.quote: it can be obtained from SAED pattern (as shown in Fig. 3d) that the formed Cr-rich particles in the sample CR0-A T-873-1 are coherent with the HEA matrix.

attributes.morphology: high density of dislocations and dislocation tangles

evidence.quote: Fig. 3a shows a bright field TEM image of the cold rolled sample (CR0), showing a high density of the dislocations and dislocation tangles.

phases_and_microstructures.name: partial recrystallization
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K

evidence.quote: After annealed at 873 K and 923 K, the FeCrCoMnNi alloy was partially recrystallized, with the average grain size in the recrystallization regions being ~ 4 µm and ~ 8 µm, respectively.

phases_and_microstructures.name: partial recrystallization
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 923 K

evidence.quote: After annealed at 873 K and 923 K, the FeCrCoMnNi alloy was partially recrystallized, with the average grain size in the recrystallization regions being ~ 4 µm and ~ 8 µm, respectively.

phases_and_microstructures.name: nanotwin
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 923 K

evidence.quote: Increasing the annealing temperature to 923 K (sample CR0-A T-923-1), more recrystallized grains with nanotwins can be observed, and the insert SAED pattern shows the typical FCC twin structure with zone axis ] 12 1 [ (Fig. 3e).

phases_and_microstructures.name: fully recrystallized grain
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 973 K

evidence.quote: The average grain sizes of the CR0-A T-973-1, CR0-A T-1073-1 and CR0-A T-1173-1 are ~ 8 µm, ~ 10 µm and ~ 20 µm, respectively.

phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 973 K

attributes.morphology: step-like twin boundary with ITB and CTB

evidence.quote: The “step-like” twin boundary with both incoherent twin boundary (ITB) and coherent twin boundary (CTB) was observed in Fig. 3f

phases_and_microstructures.name: fully recrystallized grain

evidence.quote: The average grain sizes of the CR0-A T-973-1, CR0-A T-1073-1 and CR0-A T-1173-1 are ~ 8 µm, ~ 10 µm and ~ 20 µm, respectively.

evidence.quote: The average grain sizes of the CR0-A T-973-1, CR0-A T-1073-1 and CR0-A T-1173-1 are ~ 8 µm, ~ 10 µm and ~ 20 µm, respectively.

phases_and_microstructures.name: heterogeneous structure
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 923 K

attributes.morphology: nanotwins in recrystallized grains and high density of dislocations in deformed regions

evidence.quote: As the annealing temperature is between 873~973 K, the annealed samples develop heterogeneous structure that comprise nanotwins in the recrystallized grains and a high density of the dislocations in the deformed regions.

phases_and_microstructures.name: shear band
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 773 K, after tensile to failure

evidence.quote: Shear bands were observed in the sample CR0-A T-773-1 after tensile to failure, as shown in Fig. 5a.

phases_and_microstructures.name: dislocation wall
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K, after tensile to failure

evidence.quote: Fig. 5b shows the formed dislocation walls in the sample CR0-A T-873-1.

phases_and_microstructures.name: dislocation cell
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 923 K, after tensile to failure

evidence.quote: A high density of dislocation cells can be observed in the samples CR0-A T-923-1 and CR0-A T-1173-1 after tensile to failure (as shown in Fig. 5c and 5d), and the average size of the dislocation cells is less than 100 nm.

property_observations.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 773 K

evidence.quote: The following annealing treatment at 773 K for 1 h results in additional increase of the yield stress to 1300 MPa and the alloy becomes completely brittle.

property_observations.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K

evidence.quote: With increasing the annealing temperature to 873 K, the yield stress decreases to 1050 MPa with partial recovery of the ductility to ~8%.

evidence.quote: The annealing treatments at 923, 973, 1073 and 1173 K lead to obvious ductility recovery with the yield stress decreases to 560 MPa, 520 MPa, 320 MPa and 280 MPa, respectively.

property_observations.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 973 K

evidence.quote: The annealing treatments at 923, 973, 1073 and 1173 K lead to obvious ductility recovery with the yield stress decreases to 560 MPa, 520 MPa, 320 MPa and 280 MPa, respectively.

property_observations.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 1173 K

evidence.quote: The annealing treatments at 923, 973, 1073 and 1173 K lead to obvious ductility recovery with the yield stress decreases to 560 MPa, 520 MPa, 320 MPa and 280 MPa, respectively.

mechanisms.name: precipitation strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K

evidence.quote: The precipitation phase and/or long-range ordered structure dispersely distributed inside the alloys can significantly enhance the strength, because these structures can severely block the dislocation motions [28].
The formation of Cr-rich precipitation phase in the sample CR0-A T-873-1 contributes to the high yield stress.

mechanisms.name: ordering strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 773 K

evidence.quote: the deformed dislocation substructures in the sample CR0-A T-773-1 remains almost unchanged, accompanied by the formation of long-range ordered structure inside the grains, which results in additional hardening and strengthening of the alloy with a complete sacrifice of the ductility.

mechanisms.name: back-stress strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 923 K

evidence.quote: The heterogeneous structure can produce significant back-stress during deformation. The back-stress contributes to the strength of the materials and increases the work hardening ability simultaneously that also contributes to the ductility [29].

mechanisms.name: dislocation wall formation
mechanisms.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 873 K, after tensile to failure

evidence.quote: Fig. 5b shows the formed dislocation walls in the sample CR0-A T-873-1.

mechanisms.name: dislocation cell formation
mechanisms.material_state: cold rolled and annealed at 923 K, after tensile to failure

evidence.quote: A high density of dislocation cells can be observed in the samples CR0-A T-923-1 and CR0-A T-1173-1 after tensile to failure (as shown in Fig. 5), and the average size of the dislocation cells is less than 100 nm. This would explain the high strain hardening rate and good ductility of the recrystallized samples.
